newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - August 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - August 1.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Friday:
- Record damages of 300,000 Irish punts were made to former minister Prionsias de Rossa in his lengthy High Court action against Independent Newspapers.
- The share of income tax going to pay interest on the 30 billion punt national debt halved in the past 10 years and will fall significantly more.
- Decision on U2 concerts to be handed down today.
- Ireland's finance minister Charlie McCreevy said that the governement, like its precedessor, was committed to joing EMU from day one, even if sterling did not.
- State gains 6.0 million punts in 57 million sale of Aldiscon to Logica Group.
- Sparkling AIB interims of 242 million set shares alight.
- Sellers dominate as the Irish pound comes under new pressure.
- Journalist Eamon Dunphy is due before the High Court on Tuesday to explain remarks he made on Radio Ireland in connection with the De Rossa case.
- Teenagers in Ireland and Britian have been contaminated by radioactive leaks from Sellafield in the latest cancer scare.
- Green Property Group profits up 90 percent.
- British Airways ready to challenge low-cost operators.
- Busy trade as AIB results spark bull run on bourse.
- Dana makes recommended takeover offer for Seafield.
